q: The Cramér–Rao bound states that for any unbiased estimator T̂(X) of θ:
opts: Var(T̂) ≥ 1/I(θ) where I(θ) is the Fisher information
exp: Cramér–Rao: Var(T̂(X)) ≥ 1/I(θ). The Fisher information I(θ) bounds how precisely θ can be estimated. The bound is achieved by the MLE (asymptotically) for exponential families. This is a fundamental limit on estimation precision.
